clue.text: Legendary bird old company used in grotesque ornamentation

parts.note: the roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A mythical bird and an old firm turn up in some fantastically fussy decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' is only a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth-century style is famous for elaborate, florid, often fantastical decoration of scrolls and shells.

clue.text: Note v. Nice inn sadly becoming problematic

indicators.note: sadly suggests the words are knocked about and come out in a new, sorry order

parts.note: v. is the short form of versus, giving V

explanation.surface: A traveller writes a note complaining that a nice inn has unhappily become troublesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' tells you to rearrange NOTE, V, NICE and INN together; 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inconvenient causes difficulty or trouble, which is what problematic describes.

clue.text: I married girl — boo, horrible entanglement!

indicators.note: horrible suggests the following letters are made a mess of and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone groans that marrying a girl has led to an awful, booed tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' looks like a comment on the booing, but it is the signal to rearrange the two words after 'girl'; 'married' is the crossword M.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a complicated, confused situation or tangle, especially a messy dispute.

clue.text: Country girl carries vessel on head

indicators.note: in a down clue the vessel is placed on top, at the head of the girl's name

parts.note: a can is a container, a kind of vessel
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A country girl balances a container on her head, as water carriers do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' just links; 'on head' puts CAN above ADA in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a North American nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Tatty heel darned at end — using these?

definitions.text: Tatty heel darned at end — using these?

indicators.note: tatty means worn and ragged, signalling that the words that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ragged sock heel finally gets mended, and the clue asks what tools did the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tatty' rearranges HEEL DARNED AT END; the whole clue then asks what you would darn a tatty heel with.
explanation.definitionFit: Darning a hole in a sock is done by sewing with a threaded needle, so these are the tools used.

clue.text: Finished without pax, unfortunately blown up

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for finished goes round the other piece

parts.note: something ended is finished

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters of pax are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A peace deal ends badly and things blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the word for finished wraps the jumbled letters made from 'pax' by 'unfortunately'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blown up, like a balloon, has been inflated and so has grown larger.

clue.text: Fool I spot, one to be taken in

indicators.note: to be taken in means one piece is placed inside the word for spot

parts.note: a dot is a small spot
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone says they can spot a fool, one easily duped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be taken in' puts I (one) inside DOT, after the clue's own I.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, a simpleton or dolt.

clue.text: Difficulty is seen in fine distinction

indicators.note: seen in means the small word is placed inside the word for a fine distinction

parts.note: a nuance is a subtle shade of difference

explanation.surface: A difficulty becomes clear only when one looks at a subtle difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' places the clue's own 'is' inside the word for a fine distinction; 'Difficulty' is the definition, in the sense of a source of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is an annoyance or trouble, something that causes difficulty.

clue.text: What may be sat on in class

explanation.surface: Pupils perched on benches during a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the two definitions; FORM is the British word for a school class or year group, and also a long backless bench.
explanation.definitionFit: A form is a long wooden bench for sitting, and in British schools a class or year group of pupils.

clue.text: Old lover allowed to keep quiet, that's clear

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
P stands for piano, the musical direction for quiet
licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: A former partner is told to keep quiet, and the message is unmistakable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' has the word for allowed hold the musical P for quiet, after the former partner; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit means stated plainly and in detail, leaving nothing unclear or implied.

clue.text: Fellow tucking into pumpkin? Big eater!

indicators.note: tucking into means the word for fellow goes inside the word for pumpkin

parts.note: a pumpkin is a type of gourd
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man digs into a pumpkin pie and is called a glutton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating, which suits the big eater, but it is a container signal putting the fellow inside the pumpkin's family name.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand is a glutton, someone fond of eating large amounts of food.

clue.text: Fair band to regroup

indicators.note: regroup suggests the letters are arranged into a different formation

explanation.surface: A music group splits up and gets back together in a reasonably decent state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regroup' rearranges BAND and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Not bad means reasonably good or passable, much as a fair performance is middling but acceptable.

clue.text: Old country workshop needs a boss to make good progress

parts.note: a forge is the traditional village blacksmith's workshop
a head is the person in charge

explanation.surface: A traditional blacksmith's shop needs a manager in order to grow its business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To forge ahead is to move forward steadily and strongly, advancing well.

clue.text: Lure of some authentic enchantress

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A genuine sorceress has a certain seductive appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; the run spans the end of 'authentic' and the start of 'enchantress'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to tempt or attract someone, often with an offer, which is what luring is.

clue.text: A bridge club with a high status maybe

definitions.text: A bridge club with a high status maybe

parts.words: A bridge club with a high status maybe
parts.note: read as a social club for card players, but in the game of bridge a club, if clubs are the chosen suit, outranks every other card

explanation.surface: An exclusive card-players' society with lofty standing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a society where bridge is played; in fact it means one card in the game, a club when clubs are the ruling suit, which beats any card of another suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A card of the ruling suit beats all others, and figuratively it is a decisive advantage held in reserve.

clue.text: In wild area vole's destroyed plant

indicators.note: in wild suggests the letters run riot and are rearranged
destroyed says the letters are wrecked and put back in another order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: In the countryside, a vole's burrow is wrecked and a plant is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In wild' and 'destroyed' both signal rearranging AREA and VOLE; the possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera is a succulent whose sap is used in soothing gels, a species of the aloe genus.

clue.text: Sleepy in extremis? Then have a nap in church council!

indicators.note: in extremis, read literally as at the extremes, takes only the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: to nod or nod off is to doze briefly

explanation.surface: A drowsy cleric drops off during a tedious church meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in extremis' normally means in dire straits; here it takes the outside letters of 'Sleepy'. 'Then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy and church members meeting to decide church matters.

clue.text: Disciplinarian applying cane to learner with little hesitation

parts.note: a cane is a stick
L is the learner driver's plate
er is the small sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A strict teacher hesitates only briefly before caning a pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applying ... to' and 'with' are links lining the pieces up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists rigidly on rules or standards, as a strict enforcer of discipline does.

clue.text: Gangster and thug totally forceful

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster
a lout is an aggressive, uncouth man

explanation.surface: A mobster and his heavy are utterly violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-out effort is one using every possible resource and strength, completely vigorous.

clue.text: Wartime restriction beginning and ending with international agreement

indicators.note: beginning takes a run of letters from the start of the first word
ending with takes a run of letters from the close of the second word

explanation.surface: A wartime restriction is brought in and lifted by an international treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' takes INTERN, the start of 'international', and 'ending with' takes MENT, the end of 'agreement'. 'International agreement' looks like a treaty, but the two words are worked on separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Internment is the confinement of enemy aliens or suspects without trial, a measure typical of wartime.

clue.text: Bumpkin of a brownish hue in charge

parts.note: rust is a reddish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A country yokel with a ruddy complexion is put in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic is an unsophisticated country person, like a yokel.

clue.text: Short name, indicator that is limited

parts.note: N is the short form of name
an arrow is a sign pointing the way

explanation.surface: An abbreviated name and a signpost leave little room for manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow means restricted in range or scope, as in a narrow outlook.

clue.text: Football team giving room approval from what we hear

indicators.note: from what we hear says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a cell is a small room, and a tick is a mark of approval

explanation.surface: A football club welcomes a new room, approved by its supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: CELTIC is a Glasgow football club; said aloud, CELL TICK sounds like it. 'giving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Celtic is a famous Scottish club, one of Glasgow's two big professional sides.

clue.text: Into river finally scatter ashes maybe

indicators.note: Into means the selected letter goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England

indicators.note: finally takes just the closing letter of the word scatter

explanation.surface: Someone scatters a loved one's ashes into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' puts R, the last letter of 'scatter', inside TEES. 'ashes' suggests cremation but means ash trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The ash is a common woodland species, so ashes are examples of the plants in a wood.

clue.text: All others wanting parish priest to provide relaxing remedy

parts.note: the rest means everyone else
a curé is a French parish priest

explanation.surface: Everyone else needs a parish priest to supply calming treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' and 'to provide' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest cure is a treatment of prolonged rest and quiet, a therapy for stress or exhaustion.

clue.text: Vile leer sent out a sort of signal

indicators.note: sent out suggests the letters are dispatched and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A nasty leering look is transmitted as a kind of message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent out' rearranges VILE and LEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle call sounded in the morning to wake soldiers, a military call.

clue.text: Criminal decapitated bird

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the opening letter, is cut off

parts.note: a crook is a criminal

explanation.surface: A villain beheaded a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like an adjective but is the noun CROOK.
explanation.definitionFit: The rook is a black, gregarious member of the crow family.

clue.text: Like items from factory dumped across ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed up, so the letters are broken down and remixed

explanation.surface: Goods tipped out of a factory and spilt over the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' (crushed) rearranges DUMPED ACROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Factory goods are typically made in huge numbers by standardised processes.
